---
title: "Human intent routing"
---

Every meaningful turn begins with a human intention: what the person wants to
understand, change, make, or preserve. Software is one possible response; it is
not the default container for the intention.

Create the intention specification with `$speckit-specify`. The project-local
Spec Kit template records the goal, uncertainty, constraints, completion rule,
and route. Select the smallest route that can complete the intention.

| Route | Use when the human intends to | Completion evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Document stewardship | improve an explanation, README, or manual | reviewed edit and relevant render or check |
| Learning | develop understanding or a practical skill | learner-produced explanation, exercise, or reflection |
| Preservation investigation | answer an empirical question about a device or ecosystem | approved experiment spec, observation artifacts, and an evaluated result |
| Software development | create or change software because it is the right response | Spec Kit plan, tasks, implementation, tests, and convergence |

## When an experiment may run

An experiment is not authorized by curiosity alone, nor by a Manual page. Its
intention specification must select **preservation investigation** and state:

1. the question and scope;
2. safety invariants and stop conditions;
3. the device and host in scope;
4. the observations and files expected from the run;
5. the rule for evaluating the result; and
6. `Execution status: ready to run`.

The corresponding Manual page then supplies the visible procedure, local
artifacts, and check. If the outcome suggests software, begin a new
software-development intention rather than silently extending the experiment.
